info.title: Offramp
info.description: The off-ramp from .NET Framework: deterministic analysis, pure file moves, dependency consolidation, and scaffolding for incremental migrations of large .NET Framework codebases to modern .NET.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Offramp: the off-ramp from .NET Framework. Deterministic analysis, pure moves, and scaffolding for incremental migrations to modern .NET.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --target
options.description: Integer major version of the modern target (10 = net10.0). Default: config target (10).

options.name: --solution
options.description: The .sln/.slnx/.slnf to work on; required when more than one exists.

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Workspace model to read. Default: .offramp/workspace.json.

options.name: --config
options.description: Configuration file. Default: offramp.yml at the repository root.

options.name: --json
options.description: JSON envelope on stdout, NDJSON progress on stderr, no colors. [default: False]

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the primary output (JSON, HTML, DOT, plan files) to a file.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would change without changing anything (the default for commands that modify the repository). [default: False]

options.name: --apply
options.description: Perform the changes. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Skip interactive confirmations (implied when not a terminal). [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: No progress; only the result and errors. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Debug detail on stderr. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Ignore .offramp/cache/. [default: False]

options.name: --no-llm
options.description: Never call an LLM (the default unless llm.enabled is set). [default: False]

options.name: --llm
options.description: Allow LLM garnish (naming, ranking) for this run. [default: False]

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: Exit 1 when any diagnostic is at or above this level. [default: error]

options.name: --fail-on-stale
options.description: Treat a stale workspace model (OFR0002) as an error. [default: False]

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check SDKs, reference assemblies, git, offramp.yml, the workspace model, Windows-only build steps, and central package management, and explain how to fix what is wrong.

options.name: --fix
options.description: Show the compile-only block for Windows-only build steps as a diff to Directory.Build.props; with --apply, write it. [default: False]

commands.name: init
commands.description: Write offramp.yml with detected values (interviews on a terminal) and add Offramp's state to .gitignore.

options.name: --defaults
options.description: Write the detected configuration without asking. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Replace an existing offramp.yml. [default: False]

commands.name: guide
commands.description: Walk through the migration one step at a time: explains each step, runs Offramp's commands for you, remembers progress in .offramp/guide.json, and asks when there is a choice.

options.name: --run
options.description: Run a step's command now: a dry run for steps that change the repository, unless --apply.

options.name: --done
options.description: Record a step as done without running it.

options.name: --skip
options.description: Record a step as skipped.

options.name: --reset
options.description: Forget what was recorded for a step, or `all` to start the guide's record over.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project, for a step done per project (path or name).

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Build the workspace model (.offramp/workspace.json) from a build of the solution or from logs, and record a ledger snapshot.

options.name: --binlog
options.description: Read an existing MSBuild binary log instead of building (for example one captured on Windows).

options.name: --complog
options.description: Use a compiler log (from `complog create`). Alone it gives a reduced model; with --binlog, the full one.

options.name: --if-stale
options.description: Rescan only when the model is stale. [default: False]

options.name: --no-build
options.description: Reuse the previous scan's binary log instead of building. [default: False]

commands.name: slice
commands.description: Write a solution filter (.slnf) for a project closure so a slice of a large repository builds quickly.

options.name: --for
options.description: Projects to slice around: repository-relative paths or project names, comma-separated or repeated.

options.name: --include-dependents
options.description: Also include every project that depends on them. [default: False]

options.name: --include-tests
options.description: Also include test projects that reference anything in the slice. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: slnf: a solution filter; slngen: a SlnGen command line. [default: slnf]

commands.name: graph
commands.description: Show the project dependency graph with framework class and kind, as data, DOT, Mermaid, or a self-contained interactive HTML page.

options.name: --format
options.description: json (the graph data), dot, mermaid, or html. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --exclude-kind
options.description: Leave out projects of these kinds, for example test. Comma-separated or repeated.

options.name: --include-kind
options.description: Show only projects of these kinds. Comma-separated or repeated.

options.name: --focus
options.description: Show the subgraph around this project (path or name).

options.name: --depth
options.description: Levels around --focus (default: all).

options.name: --direction
options.description: Around --focus: both, dependencies, or dependents. [default: both]

options.name: --cluster
options.description: Group projects: none, directory, or kind. [default: none]

options.name: --highlight
options.description: Mark cycles, the frontier (ready to port today), the top blockers, or none. [default: cycles]

options.name: --edges
options.description: all, or project to hide HintPath references to other projects' outputs. [default: all]

commands.name: deps
commands.description: Package and assembly dependencies: what supports the target, and what to do about the rest.

commands.name: audit
commands.description: For every package in use: which versions support the target, the lowest and newest that do, and what blocks the rest.

options.name: --package
options.description: Audit only this package.

options.name: --project
options.description: Audit only what this project uses (path or name).

options.name: --include-prerelease
options.description: Consider prerelease versions (deps.includePrerelease). [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), or markdown. [default: table]

commands.name: consolidate
commands.description: One version per package across the solution, respecting pins, families, and transitive constraints, verified by NuGet's own restore.

options.name: --package
options.description: Consolidate this package (and the rest of its family).

options.name: --all
options.description: Consolidate every package referenced directly. [default: False]

options.name: --family
options.description: Consolidate the packages whose id starts with this prefix.

options.name: --prefer
options.description: lowest (default) or newest version that satisfies every constraint (deps.preferNewest).

options.name: --cpm
options.description: Move versions into a central props file (deps.cpm.file) with central package management. [default: False]

options.name: --opt-in-via
options.description: With a non-default central file, opt projects in through this shared props file instead of each project.

options.name: --verify
options.description: restore (default): NuGet restores the proposal in a scratch copy first; build: then build it too; none. [default: restore]

commands.name: gac
commands.description: .NET Framework assembly references and their modern equivalents, with how much each is used.

options.name: --project
options.description: Only this project (path or name).

commands.name: resolve-dlls
commands.description: Replace References with a HintPath by the project that builds the DLL or the package that ships it; report the rest.

options.name: --project
options.description: Only this project (path or name).

commands.name: report
commands.description: Summarize migration progress for stakeholders: headline numbers, the burn-down across scans, applications, and what can be ported today.

options.name: --format
options.description: html (a self-contained page), json (the data behind the charts), or markdown. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --since
options.description: Start the burn-down at this date (2026-09-01) or UTC time.

options.name: --title
options.description: The page title (default: report.title, else the repository folder's name).

options.name: --with-graph
options.description: Embed the interactive dependency graph (HTML only). [default: False]

commands.name: plan
commands.description: Order the migration leaf-first: what can be ported today, what each project waits on, and how far each change reaches.

options.name: --frontier
options.description: Only projects that can be ported today: every dependency is already portable. [default: False]

options.name: --for
options.description: Only what must be ported for this project to run on the target (path or name).

options.name: --waves
options.description: Group the order into waves; each wave depends only on earlier ones. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude-kind
options.description: Leave out projects of these kinds, for example test. Comma-separated or repeated.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Build the affected projects with the repository's own toolchain (or run verify.command) and report new errors, grouped by code.

options.name: --projects
options.description: Verify these projects (paths or names), comma-separated or repeated.

options.name: --affected-by
options.description: Verify the projects owning these changed files or folders, and their direct dependents.

options.name: --all
options.description: Verify every project (the default unless verify.projects.include is set). [default: False]

options.name: --mode
options.description: build, command, or none (default: verify.mode).

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Record the current errors as the baseline; later runs fail only on errors it does not list. [default: False]

commands.name: move
commands.description: Move code between projects without changing a byte of it: renames are staged with git mv, project edits left for review.

commands.name: plan
commands.description: Plan a move of files between projects: what moves, what comes along, which references to add, and what stays and why. Changes nothing.

options.name: --from
options.description: The project the files are in (path or name).

options.name: --to
options.description: The project to move them to (path or name).

options.name: --files
options.description: Files to move: paths or globs (relative to the current directory), matched against the source project's files.

options.name: --files-from
options.description: A file listing paths to move, one per line (# starts a comment).

options.name: --all
options.description: Plan every file of the source project. [default: False]

options.name: --co-move
options.description: closure (default, from move.coMove): bring along what the files need; none: exclude them instead.

options.name: --namespace-mismatch
options.description: allow (default, from move.namespaceMismatch), warn, or block files outside the destination's root namespace.

commands.name: apply
commands.description: Apply a move plan: project edits, then pure renames (git mv), each journaled; verify, and roll back on failure.

options.name: --plan
options.description: The plan written by move plan --out.

options.name: --verify
options.description: When to verify: end (default, from the plan), none, per-project, or batch:N (every N files).

options.name: --on-failure
options.description: rollback (default, from verify.onFailure) undoes the whole run; keep leaves it for inspection.

options.name: --resume
options.description: Finish this plan's interrupted run from its journal. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Apply a plan made from a different workspace model. [default: False]

commands.name: tests
commands.description: Find test code in a production project and move it, byte for byte, to its test project.

options.name: --project
options.description: The production project holding tests (path or name).

options.name: --to
options.description: The test project to move them to (default: the project named <Name>.Tests).

options.name: --create
options.description: Create <Name>.Tests next to the project when no test project exists. [default: False]

options.name: --include-helpers
options.description: Move helpers down to this confidence: high (default, from move.tests.helperMinConfidence), medium, low, or none.

options.name: --prune-packages
options.description: Remove the project's test-framework packages when nothing left in it uses them. [default: False]

options.name: --apply
options.description: Perform the move. Without it, show the plan and the project-file diff (dry run). [default: False]

options.name: --verify
options.description: Verify after applying: end (default, from move.verify) or none.

commands.name: rollback
commands.description: Undo an applied move from its journal: renames reversed, project files restored byte for byte, new files deleted.

options.name: --journal
options.description: The journal an applied move wrote (.offramp/journal/...).

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Move types into a new project: create it from a template (the source's settings, analyzers, and framework references), then plan and apply the move.

options.name: --from
options.description: The project the types are in (path or name).

options.name: --types
options.description: Types to move, fully qualified or by a unique name; comma-separated or repeated.

options.name: --files
options.description: Files to move: paths or globs (relative to the current directory), matched against the source project's files.

options.name: --new
options.description: The new project's name; its file is NAME.csproj.

options.name: --tfm
options.description: Its target frameworks, semicolon-separated (default: the source's).

options.name: --dir
options.description: Its folder (default: NAME beside the source project's folder).

options.name: --verify
options.description: With --apply: none, end (default, from move.verify), per-project, or batch:N.

commands.name: forwarders
commands.description: Keep binary consumers working after types moved: write TypeForwardedTo attributes in the source for types now in the destination, and report strings that name them with the old assembly.

options.name: --from
options.description: The project the types moved out of (path or name).

options.name: --to
options.description: The project they moved to (path or name).

options.name: --since
options.description: Read the source's former public types at this commit (default: the compilation of the last scan).

commands.name: redirects
commands.description: Binding redirects for .NET Framework applications.

commands.name: sync
commands.description: Rewrite the assemblyBinding section of app.config/web.config from the resolved package graph; everything else in the file stays byte for byte.

options.name: --app
options.description: The application project to sync (path or name; repeatable). Default: every .NET Framework application.

options.name: --prune
options.description: Remove redirects for assemblies no package in the graph provides. [default: False]

commands.name: audit
commands.description: Read-only code audits: what will not compile or will throw on the target, what behaves differently, binary serialization, and native interop.

commands.name: api
commands.description: APIs missing on the target (compiling each .NET Framework project against the target's reference assemblies), Windows-only APIs, APIs that throw, and removed technologies; with a porting ledger.

options.name: --project
options.description: Audit only these projects (path or name). Repeatable.

options.name: --pack
options.description: Run only these rule packs (core, web, desktop, data, serialization, native). Repeatable; overrides rules.packs.disable.

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), sarif, or markdown. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: Group findings by rule, project, namespace, or file. [default: rule]

options.name: --all-locations
options.description: List every location (default: the first 5 per group). [default: False]

commands.name: behavior
commands.description: Code that compiles on the target but behaves differently: culture, encodings, paths, time zones, the registry, ambient contexts, and more.

options.name: --project
options.description: Audit only these projects (path or name). Repeatable.

options.name: --pack
options.description: Run only these rule packs (core, web, desktop, data, serialization, native). Repeatable; overrides rules.packs.disable.

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), sarif, or markdown. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: Group findings by rule, project, namespace, or file. [default: rule]

options.name: --all-locations
options.description: List every location (default: the first 5 per group). [default: False]

commands.name: serialization
commands.description: BinaryFormatter and its relatives: whether the data stays in the process (a deep clone) or outlives it, and which types it carries.

options.name: --project
options.description: Audit only these projects (path or name). Repeatable.

options.name: --pack
options.description: Run only these rule packs (core, web, desktop, data, serialization, native). Repeatable; overrides rules.packs.disable.

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), sarif, or markdown. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: Group findings by rule, project, namespace, or file. [default: rule]

options.name: --all-locations
options.description: List every location (default: the first 5 per group). [default: False]

commands.name: native
commands.description: P/Invoke inventory, marshalling defaults that differ, LibraryImport candidates, and COM.

options.name: --project
options.description: Audit only these projects (path or name). Repeatable.

options.name: --pack
options.description: Run only these rule packs (core, web, desktop, data, serialization, native). Repeatable; overrides rules.packs.disable.

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), sarif, or markdown. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: Group findings by rule, project, namespace, or file. [default: rule]

options.name: --all-locations
options.description: List every location (default: the first 5 per group). [default: False]

commands.name: dead-code
commands.description: Types and members nothing in the solution references, with a confidence level and its evidence, and the lines that would go away.

options.name: --scope
options.description: public (symbols visible outside their assembly) or all. [default: all]

options.name: --min-confidence
options.description: Report candidates at this confidence or above: high, medium, or low. [default: low]

options.name: --include-tests
options.description: Report production code only test projects use (OFR3402) instead of counting those uses. [default: False]

options.name: --project
options.description: Only candidates declared in these projects (path or name). Repeatable; references are still read solution-wide.

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), or markdown. [default: table]

commands.name: api-compat
commands.description: Compare the public API of a project's two targets, or of the working tree and a git revision, with Microsoft's ApiCompat.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project to compare (path or name).

options.name: --left
options.description: Left target framework (default: the first .NET Framework target).

options.name: --right
options.description: Right target framework (default: the newest modern target).

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Compare the working tree with the build at this git revision instead.

commands.name: ifdef
commands.description: Conditional compilation that bridges targets: how much there is, wrapping audit findings in #if, and stripping regions when a target is dropped.

commands.name: report
commands.description: Count #if regions and the lines inside them, per symbol and project.

options.name: --symbol
options.description: Only regions whose conditions name this symbol (NETFRAMEWORK, NET10_0_OR_GREATER, ...).

commands.name: wrap
commands.description: Wrap the statements or members behind audit findings in #if … #endif, inserting whole lines only; members code on every target needs are left for a real port (OFR3601).

options.name: --findings
options.description: An audit result: the output of `offramp audit api --format json` (or its --json envelope).

options.name: --symbol
options.description: The condition to write after #if (NETFRAMEWORK, or !NET10_0_OR_GREATER). [default: NETFRAMEWORK]

commands.name: strip
commands.description: Remove the #if regions that name a symbol, keeping the branch selected by --keep; regions that also depend on other symbols stay (OFR3603).

options.name: --symbol
options.description: The symbol whose regions go (NETFRAMEWORK when net48 is dropped).

options.name: --keep
options.description: Keep the branch for the symbol defined (true) or not defined (false). [default: false]

commands.name: seams
commands.description: Find the smallest boundary around code that cannot port: tainted types, the minimum cut, and the interfaces to extract.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project to find seams in (path or name).

options.name: --unportable-from
options.description: audit (run audit api on the project; default from seams.unportableSources) or list (only --symbols and seams.unportableSymbols).

options.name: --symbols
options.description: Namespaces or types that cannot port (comma-separated or repeated), added to seams.unportableSymbols.

options.name: --max-cut
options.description: Report no seam when the smallest boundary crosses more references than this.

options.name: --format
options.description: table, json, dot, or html. Inferred from --out's extension when omitted.

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Edits that cut a dependency: put an interface between callers and a type that cannot port.

commands.name: interface
commands.description: Generate an interface next to a type with the members its callers use, implement it, and retype the callers' injected dependencies to it; compiled in memory before anything is written.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project that declares the type (path or name).

options.name: --type
options.description: The class to extract from, fully qualified. Defaults to the seam's boundary type with --from-seams.

options.name: --name
options.description: The interface name. Defaults to the seam's proposed name, or I + the type's name.

options.name: --members
options.description: Member names to put on the interface (comma-separated or repeated); default every public instance member.

options.name: --from-seams
options.description: A seam from `offramp seams --out seams.json`, as FILE#ID: its members and callers.

options.name: --di
options.description: The registration snippet to print: microsoft, autofac, or none. [default: microsoft]

commands.name: remote
commands.description: Turn a seam interface into an HTTP boundary: a contracts project, a Windows host that runs the implementation, and a client that implements the interface by calling the host.

options.name: --interface
options.description: The interface to put on the network, fully qualified (from extract interface).

options.name: --implementation
options.description: The class the host runs; default the one class in the project that implements the interface.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project that declares the interface (path or name); default the project whose sources declare it.

options.name: --host-framework
options.description: auto (net10.0-windows when the implementation compiles for it, else net48), net10-windows, or net48. [default: auto]

options.name: --transport
options.description: http-json (POST per member). gRPC is planned (docs/decisions/0023). [default: http-json]

options.name: --serializer
options.description: The client's JSON serializer: stj (System.Text.Json) or newtonsoft. [default: stj]

options.name: --host-dir
options.description: Where the host project goes (default next to the project: NAME.Windows.Host).

options.name: --client-dir
options.description: Where the client project goes (default NAME.Remote).

options.name: --contracts-dir
options.description: Where the contracts project goes (default NAME.Remote.Contracts).

options.name: --container
options.description: Also write a Windows Dockerfile and a Kubernetes Deployment and Service for the host. [default: False]

options.name: --async-variant
options.description: Also generate INameAsync (Task-returning members with cancellation) implemented by the client. [default: False]

options.name: --skip-member
options.description: Interface members that stay local: the client throws NotSupportedException for them (comma-separated or repeated).

commands.name: service
commands.description: Turn a Windows service (ServiceBase or Topshelf) into a worker for the generic host: a Linux container, a Windows service, or both.

options.name: --project
options.description: The Windows service's project (path or name).

options.name: --host
options.description: linux (a container), windows (a Windows service), or both. [default: linux]

options.name: --out
options.description: The worker project's directory (default NAME.Worker next to the project).

options.name: --dockerfile
options.description: Also write a Linux Dockerfile (multi-stage, non-root). [default: False]

options.name: --k8s
options.description: Also write a Kubernetes Deployment and ConfigMap. [default: False]

options.name: --health
options.description: Serve /health with each worker's last heartbeat (the project becomes Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web). [default: False]

options.name: --logging
options.description: json-console or simple. [default: json-console]

commands.name: codemod
commands.description: Bulk, idempotent Roslyn rewrites for recurring migration patterns, with a dry-run diff and a verifying build.

commands.name: list
commands.description: The codemod catalog: IDs, names, what each rewrites, and the packages it adds.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run codemods over projects: a diff by default, --apply to write through a journal and verify with a build.

options.name: --mod
options.description: Codemods by name or ID (comma-separated or repeated); `all` is every codemod that is neither opt-in nor experimental.

options.name: --project
options.description: Projects to rewrite (path or name, repeatable); default every C# project with a recorded compilation.

options.name: --verify
options.description: After --apply: end (default) builds the changed projects and their dependents, rolling back on failure; none skips it.

options.name: --experimental
options.description: Allow experimental codemods (right less than ~95% of the time; review every change). [default: False]

options.name: --format-mode
options.description: Delegate to `dotnet format analyzers --diagnostics OFRM###` in projects that reference the Offramp.Analyzers package. [default: False]

commands.name: csproj
commands.description: Project file conversions: legacy projects to SDK style, and modern settings for all.

commands.name: modernize
commands.description: Convert legacy projects to SDK style (packages.config, globs, AssemblyInfo, build events), proved by building both and comparing what the compiler gets.

options.name: --project
options.description: Projects to modernize (path or name, repeatable).

options.name: --all
options.description: Every C# project in the workspace model. [default: False]

options.name: --tfm
options.description: Target frameworks for every modernized project, semicolon-separated (net48;net10.0).

options.name: --nullable
options.description: Set Nullable (enable, disable, warnings, annotations); left alone unless given.

options.name: --accept-diff
options.description: Apply even when the converted build compiles different inputs (OFR4303). [default: False]

commands.name: config
commands.description: Configuration conversions: App.config and Web.config to appsettings.json.

commands.name: convert
commands.description: Convert App.config or Web.config to appsettings.json, options classes, and appsettings.{Environment}.json from transforms.

options.name: --project
options.description: The project whose App.config or Web.config to convert (path or name).

options.name: --out
options.description: Where to write appsettings.json and the classes (default: next to the configuration file).

options.name: --sections
options.description: appSettings, connectionStrings, custom (every custom section), or section names; default all.

options.name: --shim
options.description: Also write ConfigurationManagerShim, ConfigurationManager's API over IConfiguration, for code that cannot take IConfiguration yet. [default: False]

commands.name: web
commands.description: ASP.NET (System.Web) applications: what they are made of, and a strangler-fig ASP.NET Core front.

commands.name: inventory
commands.description: What an ASP.NET application is made of: controllers, actions, routes, filters, modules, handlers, Global.asax, Web Forms, session, authentication, and its System.Web API surface.

options.name: --project
options.description: The ASP.NET application's project (path or name).

options.name: --format
options.description: table (the terminal view), json (the result alone), or markdown. [default: table]

commands.name: scaffold
commands.description: Strangler fig: a new ASP.NET Core application that serves the controller actions that port and sends everything else to the legacy application.

options.name: --project
options.description: The ASP.NET application's project (path or name).

options.name: --new
options.description: The new ASP.NET Core project's folder; its name is the folder's name.

options.name: --proxy
options.description: yarp (the new application proxies the rest to the legacy one) or none (an ingress does; the path list is written). [default: yarp]

options.name: --adapters
options.description: Share session and authentication with the legacy application through the System.Web adapters (remote app client). [default: False]

options.name: --legacy-url
options.description: The legacy application's URL (default: the project's IIS URL).

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Offramp for AI agents: a Model Context Protocol server.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serve every command as an MCP tool (offramp_<group>_<command>) over stdio, with the workspace model, plans, the ledger, and diagnostic documentation as resources.

options.name: --allow-apply
options.description: Honor --apply and --yes in tool calls; without it every call is a dry run. [default: False]

options.name: --root
options.description: Confine every path a tool call names to this directory, and run the tools there (default: the current directory).

commands.name: ide
commands.description: What the VS Code, Visual Studio, and Rider extensions show: new code in .NET Framework projects checked for APIs modern .NET lacks, and types that could live in a portable counterpart.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Report what the editor would show: findings on new code, new types that could live in a portable counterpart, and files that could move there. Changes nothing.

options.name: --file
options.description: Files to report on (relative to the current directory); default: every C# file changed since the new-code base.

options.name: --base
options.description: The git ref new code is compared with (its merge base with HEAD); default ide.newCode.base (auto: origin/HEAD, else HEAD).

options.name: --scope
options.description: lines (default, from ide.newCode.scope): changed lines; files: every line of a changed file; all: everything.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serve the editor integration as a Language Server Protocol server over stdio, for the IDE extensions. Logs go to stderr.

options.name: --stdio
options.description: Accepted for language clients that pass it; the server always uses stdio. [default: False]
